question.text: In the InfoGripe bulletin for epidemiological week 44 of 2026 (expected 12 November 2026), what will Brazil's national long-term SRAG trend be reported as?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves based on the national long-term trend statement in Fiocruz's "Resumo do Boletim InfoGripe – Semana Epidemiológica (SE) 44 2026" (PDF expected at https://agencia.fiocruz.br/sites/agencia.fiocruz.br/files/Resumo_InfoGripe_2026_44.pdf on 12 November 2026). It resolves to the option matching the signal that this document gives for the long-term trend, "tendência de longo prazo (últimas 6 semanas)" — typically the national bullet beginning "No cenário nacional, os casos de SRAG apresentam sinal de ...". "Decline" corresponds to queda / declínio / redução, "Stability or oscillation" to estabilização and/or oscilação, and "Growth" to aumento / crescimento / alta; the long-term signal decides regardless of the short-term ("últimas 3 semanas") signal, and if a single signal is given for both horizons it applies to the long-term trend. Hedged or transitional wording is mapped by the direction it asserts: interruption phrasing ("interrupção do crescimento", "interrupção da queda") resolves as Stability or oscillation, an asserted increase including "leve aumento" or "possível início de crescimento" resolves as Growth, and an asserted decrease including "leve queda" or "possível início de queda" resolves as Decline. If the summary contains no national long-term statement, the corresponding national long-term statement in the full InfoGripe bulletin for SE 44, or in the Agência Fiocruz de Notícias release for that edition, is used instead.
question.fine_print: The source text is in Portuguese and the Portuguese terms in the criteria are the operative ones. If the SE 44 summary is not published on 12 November 2026, resolution waits for it — or, if the SE 44 edition is skipped entirely, for the next weekly InfoGripe summary published — applying the same rule to that document's national long-term statement. Trend wording in other documents (e.g., Ministry of Health "Informe" files) does not decide the question. If the PDF is inaccessible, the InfoGripe release for that edition on Agência Fiocruz de Notícias (agencia.fiocruz.br) or [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) may be used.

research:
Bottom line: nothing settles this yet. In the latest Fiocruz bulletin (SE 42, released 29 Oct) the national long-term SRAG signal was stability/oscillation and the short-term signal was growth. The national curve has been flipping between stability and decline for weeks. One new upward push is a slight national rise in severe COVID-19, still at low levels.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-12 (expected): the SE 44 summary URL in the criteria (Resumo_InfoGripe_2026_44.pdf) is not published yet. SE 43 is due around 2026-11-05, after forecasts close.
- 2026-10-29: I fetched the SE 42 summary PDF, but the tool could not decode its text, so I could not quote it directly. The BVS Saúde Pública release for SE 42 says SRAG nationally shows "tendência de estabilização ou oscilação nas últimas seis semanas" (long term) and "aumento nas últimas três semanas" (short term). [BVS](https://saudepublica.bvs.br/2026/10/29/infogripe-cinco-estados-tem-srag-em-nivel-de-alerta-ou-risco-com-sinal-de-crescimento/)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has happened that settles or nearly settles the question. The last reading was long-term stability with short-term growth. If the short-term growth continues, it would feed into the six-week window by SE 44, though I am inferring that, not quoting a source.
- 2026-10-29 (SE 42) virus trends nationally:
  - Severe COVID-19 cases show "leve crescimento", but remain "em níveis baixos".
  - Rhinovirus is stable.
  - Metapneumovirus is falling.
  - Five states are at alert/risk level with long-term growth: Amapá, Mato Grosso, Mato Grosso do Sul, Sergipe and Maranhão. [BVS](https://saudepublica.bvs.br/2026/10/29/infogripe-cinco-estados-tem-srag-em-nivel-de-alerta-ou-risco-com-sinal-de-crescimento/), [Piranot](https://www.piranot.com.br/2026/10/30/noticias/saude-qualidade-vida/alerta-srag-cinco-estados-infogripe/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-01: Cuiabá's municipal bulletin (updated 29 Oct) reports COVID-19 notifications down 85% year on year for SE 1 to 42. This is local data and not decisive. [Circuito MT](https://circuitomt.com.br/cuiaba-registra-queda-de-853-nos-casos-de-covid-19-em-2026-aponta-secretaria-municipal-de-saude/)
- 2026-10-29/30: SE 42 coverage:
  - The number of states at alert/risk with long-term growth went up from three in SE 41 to five.
  - SARS-CoV-2 is driving SRAG growth in Mato Grosso and Mato Grosso do Sul.
  - Roraima and Santa Catarina show warning signs, but without long-term growth. [Diário do Poder](https://diariodopoder.com.br/brasil-e-regioes/e12-brasil/cinco-estados-entram-em-alerta-para-doencas-respiratorias-diz-a-fiocruz)
- 2026-10-22 (SE 41): Goiás, Mato Grosso and Sergipe had alert/risk levels with growth, with COVID-19 the main driver in Mato Grosso. [TV Prefeito](https://tvprefeito.com/infogripe-tres-estados-tem-incidencia-de-srag-em-nivel-de-alerta-ou-risco-com-sinal-de-crescimento/), [RO Acontece](https://roacontece.com.br/2026/10/22/sergipe-registra-aumento-de-casos-graves-de-doencas-respiratorias-aponta-fiocruz/)
- 2026-10-15 (SE 40): national long- and short-term trends were both stability/oscillation.
  - Metapneumovirus was the only virus growing nationally.
  - Sergipe was the only state at alert level with growth.
  - COVID-19 rose slightly in Mato Grosso, while small increases in Acre, Goiás, the Federal District and São Paulo lost strength. [Fiocruz](https://fiocruz.br/noticia/2026/10/infogripe-apenas-sergipe-tem-srag-em-nivel-de-alerta-e-tendencia-de-aumento)
- Sources disagree on SE 39: a Galícia Educação summary says long-term queda, while the Ministry of Health Informe SE 39 says estabilização/oscilação. The question background lists SE 39 as stability. [Informe SE 39](https://www.gov.br/saude/pt-br/assuntos/saude-de-a-a-z/c/covid-19/atualizacao-de-casos/informe-se-39-de-2026.pdf)

## 4. Base rates
- 2026, SE 35 to 42, national long-term signal (from the question background, partly verified above):
  - Stability/oscillation: 4 of 7 readings (SE 35, 39, 40, 42).
  - Decline: 3 of 7 (SE 36, 38, 41).
  - Growth: 0 of 7.
  - The signal changed between most consecutive readings.
- When the short-term signal was growth (SE 38 and SE 39), the long-term signal the next week was stability (SE 39) and stability (SE 40). Short-term growth did not turn into long-term growth in those cases.
- 2025 comparison:
  - October 2025: national growth on both horizons, driven by influenza A.
  - Bulletin of 27 Nov 2025: decline on both horizons. [Londrina informe](https://saude.londrina.pr.gov.br/images/Epidemiologia/DEPIS/Informe_Epidemiológico/2025/Informe_epidemiologico_112025.pdf)
  - I could not find the national statement for SE 44 of 2025 itself.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the market prices supplied match this question: the Kalshi and Polymarket lists cover GDP, inflation, elections and other unrelated topics.
- I found no prediction market or expert forecast on InfoGripe trend signals.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Around 2026-11-05 (Thursday): SE 43 bulletin, data through about 31 Oct. This is the best leading indicator: watch whether short-term growth continues and whether the long-term signal moves to growth.
- Around 2026-11-06/07: Ministry of Health Informe SE 43. It does not decide the question and has diverged from Fiocruz before.
- 2026-11-02 is the Finados holiday, which may slightly delay SIVEP-Gripe notifications. The nowcast corrects for reporting delay, but holidays can add noise (my inference).
- 2026-11-12: SE 44 summary, which decides the question.

I could not settle this question. The SE 44 summary is due 12 Nov 2026 and does not exist yet, and the SE 43 bulletin, expected around 5 Nov, is not out either. The latest national reading (SE 42) is long-term stability/oscillation with short-term growth.

### 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-02: The SE 44 PDF (Resumo_InfoGripe_2026_44.pdf) has not been published. It is expected 2026-11-12.
- 2026-10-29: I fetched the SE 42 summary PDF, but the fetch tool returned only binary data, so I could not quote its text directly. [Fiocruz PDF](https://agencia.fiocruz.br/sites/agencia.fiocruz.br/files/Resumo_InfoGripe_2026_42.pdf)
- 2026-10-29: The BVS write-up of SE 42 (data through 24 Oct) gives the national trend as "tendência de estabilização ou oscilação nas últimas seis semanas" (long-term) and "aumento nas últimas três semanas" (short-term). [BVS](https://saudepublica.bvs.br/2026/10/29/infogripe-cinco-estados-tem-srag-em-nivel-de-alerta-ou-risco-com-sinal-de-crescimento/)

### 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. The most recent long-term signal is stability/oscillation, and the short-term signal is growth.
- The SE 43 bulletin (around 2026-11-05) will be the last reading before resolution. I found no sign that it has been published.

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-01: Cuiabá reports Covid-19 notifications down 85% for weeks 1 to 42 of 2026 compared with 2025. This contrasts with InfoGripe's statewide signal that SRAG in Mato Grosso is being driven by SARS-CoV-2. [Circuito MT](https://circuitomt.com.br/cuiaba-registra-queda-de-853-nos-casos-de-covid-19-em-2026-aponta-secretaria-municipal-de-saude/)
- 2026-10-29/30 (SE 42):
  - Five states are at alert/risk level with long-term growth: Amapá, Maranhão, Mato Grosso, Mato Grosso do Sul and Sergipe.
  - National signals by virus: metapneumovirus falling, rhinovirus stable, a slight rise in severe Covid-19.
  - Covid-19 is rising in MT, MS, SP and RJ, but incidence in SP and RJ is still very low.
  - In Amapá and Maranhão there was not enough lab data to identify which virus is driving the rise.
  - [BVS](https://saudepublica.bvs.br/2026/10/29/infogripe-cinco-estados-tem-srag-em-nivel-de-alerta-ou-risco-com-sinal-de-crescimento/), [Piranot](https://www.piranot.com.br/2026/10/30/noticias/saude-qualidade-vida/alerta-srag-cinco-estados-infogripe/)
- 2026-10-22 (SE 41): Three states were at alert/risk level with growth. Reports cited a rise in metapneumovirus SRAG and a slight rise in rhinovirus and Covid-19. Five capitals were at alert or above with long-term growth: Aracaju, Cuiabá, João Pessoa, Palmas and Rio de Janeiro. [Agência Fiocruz](https://agencia.fiocruz.br/infogripe-tres-estados-tem-incidencia-de-srag-em-nivel-de-alerta-ou-risco-com-sinal-de-crescimento)
- 2026-10-15 (SE 40): Only Sergipe was at alert level with a rising trend. [BVS](https://saudepublica.bvs.br/2026/10/15/infogripe-apenas-sergipe-tem-srag-em-nivel-de-alerta-e-tendencia-de-aumento/)
- 2026-10-08 (SE 39): National signal was "oscilação ou estabilização nas últimas seis semanas" (long-term) and "crescimento ... nas últimas três semanas" (short-term). [Agência Fiocruz](https://agencia.fiocruz.br/infogripe-alerta-para-importancia-da-vacinacao-contra-covid-19-e-vsr)

### 4. Base rates
- The 2026 long-term signals for SE 35 to 42, as given in the question, were stability, decline, (SE 37 not given), decline, stability, stability, decline, stability. That is 4 stability, 3 decline and 0 growth out of 7. I independently confirmed only SE 39 and SE 42.
- The short-term signal has shown growth in 3 of the last 5 editions (SE 38, 39, 42). Growth has not yet carried through to the long-term signal.
- Same period in previous years:
  - 2025-10-09: national growth in both the short and long term, driven by influenza A. This came from a search-result summary; I did not fetch the report itself. [Agência Gov](https://agenciagov.ebc.com.br/noticias/202510/infogripe-casos-de-influenza-a-avancam-para-sao-paulo)
  - 2025-11-27: national decline in both the long and short term, according to a Londrina municipal report quoting InfoGripe. This also came from a search-result summary that I did not open. [Londrina](https://saude.londrina.pr.gov.br/images/Epidemiologia/DEPIS/Informe_Epidemiológico/2025/Informe_epidemiologico_112025.pdf)
- Earlier in 2026, nationwide long-term growth came with clear virus waves: rhinovirus in Feb/Mar and RSV in June. Right now the virus picture is mixed: metapneumovirus falling, rhinovirus flat, a slight Covid rise.

### 5. Other forecasts
- None of the supplied Kalshi or Polymarket markets are about InfoGripe or SRAG trends. They are irrelevant here.
- I found no expert or crowd forecast on this question.

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Around 2026-11-05: the SE 43 bulletin and summary (data through about 31 Oct). This is the key interim signal: if growth continues in the short term, the long-term signal may move to growth.
- 2026-11-02 was the Finados holiday. Lower notifications around that date could affect how SE 44 is nowcast.
- 2026-11-12: the SE 44 summary is published, and the question resolves from it.
- Worth watching: whether the Covid-19 rise in MT and MS, and the alerts in other states, spread into the Southeast states, which dominate the national total. In SE 42, SP and RJ Covid incidence was still very low.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** About 10 days. The SE 44 summary is expected on 12 November 2026, and the SE 43 bulletin (about 5 November) will appear after forecasts close.

(b) **Status quo:** Stability/oscillation. That was the long-term reading at SE 42 (29 October), alongside a short-term growth signal.

(c) **Base rates:** From SE 35 to SE 42, the national long-term signal was:
- Stability/oscillation: 4 of 7 readings.
- Decline: 3 of 7.
- Growth: 0 of 7.

The signal changed between most consecutive weeks. Short-term growth readings at SE 38 and SE 39 were each followed by long-term stability, not growth. In November of earlier years the national curve has sometimes risen with COVID-19 or influenza waves, but that is not reliable.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
- **29 October (SE 42):** the long-term signal was stability, the short-term signal was growth, and severe COVID-19 showed "leve crescimento" at low levels.
- **SE 41 to SE 42:** the number of states at alert/risk with long-term growth rose from 3 to 5. SARS-CoV-2 is driving growth in Mato Grosso and Mato Grosso do Sul.
- **Virus mix:** rhinovirus (53% of positives) is stable and metapneumovirus is falling, which works against a strong national rise.
- **Six-week window for SE 44:** roughly SE 39 to SE 44. It will include the recent short-term rise, which tilts the risk toward growth more than toward decline.
